correctness.rationale: Develop the positive-angle sector with angular shortest modular separation δ∈[0,alpha/2] (<π/2). The hyperbolic cosine law cosh D=cosh s cosh ρ−sinh s sinh ρ cosδ gives the minimal intrinsic distance; other windings and apex paths do not shorten this geodesic in the admissible low-angle cone. Completing the cosh radial square yields radial segment ρ± and the exact angular integral 4∫_0^min(sinh d,sinh R) sqrt(sinh²R−t²)/(1+t²)dt for R<s. Substitution t=sinh R sin u yields 2π(coshR−1) before d and 4(coshR θ−u) until apex R=s. For R≥s the radial lower endpoint becomes zero and integrating cosh ρ+−1 gives 2coshR(B+θ)−alpha−2u. The formulas coincide at R=s. As R→∞, u=O(e^-R) and θ=atan(sinh d)+O(e^-2R), giving V=G e^R−alpha+O(e^-R), G=B+atan(sinh d)=2atan(e^s tan(alpha/4)), and unique recovery s=log(tan(G/2)/tan(alpha/4)), alpha=−constant. At first-cut d=asinh(sinh s sin(alpha/2)) the two sheets form a tangent lens; the quadratic width 2ε−coth(d)y² yields (8/3)sqrt(2 tanh d)ε^(3/2). Independently evaluated radial angular integral versus closed formula in each radius regime at three different (s,alpha) pairs and checked inverse identities. The proof covers all parameters; numerical sampling is supplementary.
